claims.exact_statement: For every n>=4 and every graphical labeled degree vector d, let Omega_d be the simple undirected graphs on the fixed labeled vertex set [n] with degree vector d. The lazy chain holds with probability 1/2, otherwise chooses a four-set uniformly and one of six ordered pairs of distinct perfect matchings uniformly, and switches when the first matching is present and the second absent. The release paper states t_mix(d)<=2 n^8 in worst-case total variation distance 1/4. If |Omega_d|>1 it states spectral gap >=1/(24 n^2 binom(n,4)); if |Omega_d|=1 the mixing time is zero.
assumptions: Complete host: every vertex pair is eligible
Vertex labels and each labeled vertex degree are fixed
The degree vector is graphical and explicitly supplied
claims.status: source-reported theorem; exact statement reconstructed from pinned release PDF; source proof not independently verified
claims.novelty_boundary: The release paper claims the all-graphical-sequence simple-undirected Kannan-Tetali-Vempala result. No correctness, proof verification, external review, or priority claim is made in this audit.

costs.mixing: At most 2 n^8 lazy proposal steps for TV distance 1/4; each step samples a four-vertex set and checks at most four edges

claims.falsifier: A graphical labeled degree vector and starting graph for which the specified chain remains farther than 1/4 in total variation after 2 n^8 steps, or a source-proof defect invalidating its transition or gap argument.

claims.exact_statement: For n=2m with m>=5, split labeled cell vertices into two distant groups A and B and give each group a 4-regular circulant graph with cycle edges at distances 1 and 2. The observed disjoint union is a simple 4-regular graph with zero A-B contacts. Under the uniform degree-only law on all simple 4-regular graphs on 2m labels, permutation symmetry gives expected crossing-edge count 4m^2/(2m-1). Since the count is at most 4m, the stationary probability of at least m crossing edges is >=(2m+1)/(6m-3)>1/3. Conditional on the source mixing theorem, after 2(2m)^8 steps this event has probability >1/12 from any start, although all such cross-compartment contacts are physically impossible.
assumptions: Two compartments contain m labeled cells each and no physical cross-compartment contact is possible
Each compartment has an observed simple 4-regular contact graph
The proposed null fixes only the labeled degree vector and samples on the complete graph
Family 131's TV statement is assumed for the conditional probability consequence; its proof is not independently verified here
claims.status: internally derived exact counterexample to biological interpretation beyond the degree-only null
claims.novelty_boundary: This does not refute the chain theorem or the degree-only null as a mathematical distribution. It refutes interpreting that null as a spatially valid contact-generating model without geometry constraints.

costs.null_mixing: 2(2m)^8 proposal steps for the source TV threshold

claims.falsifier: The example's physical premise fails if cross-compartment edges are in fact feasible, or its null calculation fails if the sample space is not the complete-host uniform 4-regular graph law.

The correction branch has probability delta=2^-(4 binom(n,2)+10) and can enumerate the graph universe, so the source gives no polynomial bound on every execution.
assumptions: Input is any finite graphical labeled degree vector
Output is an exact uniform graph from the complete-host simple-undirected realization set
Expected, not worst-case per-execution, bit runtime

claims.exact_statement: Fix a labeled partition of vertices into compartments C_1,...,C_s and a within-compartment degree vector. Under H0^strat, draw each compartment graph independently and uniformly from its simple-undirected complete-host realization set with the same labeled degrees; cross-compartment edges are forbidden. For a statistic T preregistered before randomization, draw B independent null graphs G_1,...,G_B and compute p_MC=(1+#{b:T(G_b)>=T(G_0)})/(B+1). If the observed graph G_0 is itself uniform under this conditional null, G_0,...,G_B are exchangeable and p_MC is super-uniform, so rejection at p_MC<=alpha has conditional type-I error at most alpha. This is a conditional statistical application, not a new network-science theorem.
assumptions: Compartment partition, labeled degrees, node covariates, statistic, and tail direction are fixed before inspecting the observed edge pattern, or selection is otherwise accounted for
Under the null, conditional on these variables, the observed graph is uniform on the product of within-compartment degree-sequence realization sets
Each compartment host is complete within the stratum; cross-stratum edges are structurally impossible
Exact sampler outputs independent exact-uniform draws, or approximate chains are assigned an explicit joint TV error budget
claims.status: internally derived finite-sample randomization-test guarantee conditional on an explicit exchangeability null; source proof for the sampler/mixing result remains unverified
claims.novelty_boundary: The validity proof is the standard exchangeability rank argument. Family 131 supplies a source-reported sampler/mixing tool only for complete-host degree-sequence sets; it does not establish that biological observations are exchangeable or that the null generated the tissue.

costs.exact_sampler: B independent draws per compartment; expected polynomial bit cost per source corollary, but an exponentially rare correction branch and unbounded run-time tails prevent a worst-case polynomial execution guarantee
costs.approximate_switch_chain: With s strata and n_j vertices in stratum j, choose per-chain epsilon_j=eta/(B s); source t_mix(1/4)<=2 n_j^8 plus standard TV amplification gives at most 2 B ceil(log2(B s/eta)) sum_j n_j^8 proposals and type-I error at most alpha+eta; cutoff alpha-eta for eta<alpha restores at-most-alpha control
costs.Monte_Carlo_resolution: Minimum p-value 1/(B+1); B>=log(2/beta)/(2 epsilon^2) gives Hoeffding error epsilon for the fixed-threshold exceedance probability with confidence 1-beta

claims.falsifier: The test's biological calibration fails if, conditional on the asserted degrees/strata/covariates, edge opportunities remain nonexchangeable due to distance, boundaries, local density, cell type, detection, or post-hoc stratum selection; this falsifies the model interpretation, not the exchangeability lemma.
claims.next_gate: On a named dataset, preregister the compartments and molecular/contact statistic; compare complete-host, compartment-preserving, and geometry-aware local-coordinate controls, and report the spatial covariates that would falsify within-stratum exchangeability.
